titleOrRepository: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
authorsOrMaintainer: Di Wu; Hongwei Wang; Wenhao Yu; Yuwei Zhang; Kai-Wei Chang; Dong Yu
filesOrSectionsRead: Full HTML source; Abstract; Sections 3.2 (History Compilation), 3.3 (Memory Recall), 5.3 (Key: Multi-key indexing improves retrieval), and Appendix A.1-A.3 excerpts on evidence-session construction and timestamps
relevantFinding: The benchmark constructs per-question histories with evidence sessions, identifies human-annotated answer locations, and reports intermediate retrieval Recall@k and NDCG@k. It describes timestamps as manually added for temporal questions; it does not establish question_date as a universal visibility cutoff in the local JSON schema.
projectApplicability: Supports session-level candidate-to-qrel evaluation and standard Recall@k/NDCG@k reporting when original sessions and IDs are preserved.
limitations: This source does not validate raw sessions as production compressed memories, the local question_date cutoff interpretation, BM25 proxy quality, or Pareto improvement in this project.

titleOrRepository: Integrating the Probabilistic Model BM25/BM25F into Lucene
authorsOrMaintainer: Joaquín Pérez-Iglesias; José R. Pérez-Agüera; Víctor Fresno; Yuval Z. Feinstein
filesOrSectionsRead: Full HTML source; Abstract; Introduction; Included Models; BM25 scoring equation, IDF equation, and parameter description
relevantFinding: The source documents BM25 term-frequency saturation, document-length normalization, the IDF form, and Lucene's (k1+1) multiplier; the experiment freezes k1=2 and b=0.75 and applies the multiplier before bounded feature mapping.
projectApplicability: Provides a fixed, reproducible lexical relevance proxy for original sessions when no query/session embedding vectors are available locally.
limitations: The proxy is lexical and does not reproduce Qwen cosine similarity, vector-store candidate generation, semantic matching, or calibrated production similarity; the preliminary run without the multiplier is invalidated and excluded from reported evidence.

titleOrRepository: A Fast and Elitist Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm: NSGA-II
authorsOrMaintainer: Kalyanmoy Deb; Amrit Pratap; Sameer Agarwal; T. Meyarivan
license: IEEE copyrighted article; no separate permissive license stated in the mirror record
filesOrSectionsRead: Zenodo-hosted original PDF; Abstract; Section I; Section III (density estimation and crowded comparison)
relevantFinding: The reviewed text defines non-dominated sorting and a normalized crowding-distance estimate using neighboring points per objective, assigning infinite distance to boundary solutions; the crowded comparison prefers lower rank then less crowded solutions.
projectApplicability: Supports the ranking primitives used by the current Pareto candidate; it is methodological background, not a retrieval-quality result.
limitations: The two provenance records disagree on the exact sections reviewed; status is conservatively aligned to PARTIALLY_VERIFIED until that reading record is reconciled. The original paper evaluates evolutionary optimization test problems, not session retrieval, LLM memory, or this implementation's Top-K outcomes.
